A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same zeroth-order extragradient study. Their main texts, equations, Table 1, Figures 1–12, and Appendices A–E are readable and can be matched despite reflow and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E report original offline and online segmentation and clustering experiments, including comparisons with trained U-Net baselines in Table 1.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E retain original segmentation and clustering results, including numerical U-Net comparisons and adversarial-budget experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same Lovász subgradient, Gaussian two-point oracle, extragradient updates, projections, and online adaptations. Added phase comments and explanations of seed weights do not change the procedure or objectives.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic 50×50 images and moving-shape videos for segmentation, plus static and moving two-moons data for clustering. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 evaluates the same supervised and semi-supervised U-Net baselines. The newly discussed Nedić and Ozdaglar method is cited as related work but is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Data sizes, model configurations, hyperparameters, adversarial budgets, and evaluation metrics match. For example, U-Net training still uses 3,000 images, and online segmentation evaluates a three-minute, 60-fps video of 50×50 frames.

E4.justification: Both appendices contain segmentation-budget sensitivity in Figure 3, clustering-budget sensitivity in Figure 9, and online trajectory examples. The new explanatory paragraphs interpret these retained analyses without adding tests.

E5.justification: Appendix E.2 reports 10 independent runs for Algorithm 1 and relative variation on the order of 10^-4 in both versions. The added phrase describing good consistency does not change the uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 values match, including IoU values of 0.975, 0.905, and 0.847 for Algorithm 1, supervised U-Net, and semi-supervised U-Net, respectively. All twelve figures retain the same results; no result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: New Remark 3.3 combines previously documented component costs into 6n function evaluations per iteration under the theorem's one-sample setting and gives O(nm²ε⁻²) total queries. This corrects the stated query accounting; the saddle-point conditions, convergence theorems, and appendix proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction revises the offline function-query complexity claim from O(m²ε⁻²) to O(nm²ε⁻²). Claims about saddle-point convergence, the online path-length bound, novelty, and performance relative to U-Net retain their scope.

C2.justification: Appendices E.1–E.2 newly explain seed weights as enforcement, offline cost spikes through minimax interaction, and online fluctuations through a changing optimum. They distinguish convergence guarantees from monotonic objective decrease and newly interpret segmentation accuracy as evidence of near-saddle solutions without reporting duality-gap measurements.

D1.justification: v2 adds experiment-code access links in Section 4 and Appendix E, together with links to the ZoSolvers repository and Python package. v1 has no equivalent access information. Existing hardware descriptions, implementation settings, and hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: The introduction adds Nedić and Ozdaglar (2009) and discusses its first-order subgradient convergence rate. It also explains why direct comparison with Adibi et al. (2022) is inappropriate for the different submodular optimization structure. Other reference edits update bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: Localized explanations expand the introduction and Appendix E, and Algorithm 1 gains phase comments. Acknowledgements and an Impact Statement are added, alongside minor terminology, affiliation, and bibliographic edits. The overall organization of Sections 1–5 and Appendices A–E is preserved.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1's display expands with phase comments, and figures move with text reflow. For example, Figure 9 moves from page 23 to 25 and Figure 12 from page 24 to 26. Table 1 and all twelve figures retain their designs, captions, and displayed results.

improvement.justification: v2 reconciles v1's n-dependent component costs in Appendix D.1 with the advertised query complexity through Remark 3.3 and the missing n factor. Added code-access information and explanations modestly improve transparency. The benefit is tempered by the new near-saddle interpretation, which segmentation accuracy alone does not establish; the underlying empirical evidence is unchanged.
